question: How did inequality across the whole world fall after 1990 while it rose inside many rich countries?
answer: Because most global inequality lies between countries, not within them. Lakner and Milanovic showed that fast growth in China, India and other Asian economies lifted hundreds of millions toward the global middle, narrowing the gap between nations. Meanwhile gaps inside the United States or Britain widened. Both headlines were true; they measured different crowds.
move: Before arguing about a trend, ask who exactly is being compared.
ask: When I compare myself with others, which crowd am I measuring against, and why that one?
source: Lakner and Milanovic, World Bank Economic Review, 2016
reference: Lakner & Milanovic, Global Income Distribution: From the Fall of the Berlin Wall to the Great Recession, World Bank Economic Review, 2016
